summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later question-answering)

## BOOK 1: "The Movie Boys in Peril; or, Strenuous Days Along the Panama Canal" by Victor Appleton (Garden City Publishing, 1926; Gutenberg #76378)

**Main characters:** Joe Duncan and Blake Stewart ("Moving Picture Boys"; Blake is the more serious, deeper thinker; Joe is the impulsive one with a head for figures, working on a focusing-tube patent). Mr. Calvert Hadley (head of Film Theatrical Co.), Mr. Ringold (dramatic side). Film company members: C. C. Piper ("Gloomy"), Birdie Lee (Blake's sweetheart-type), Mabel Pierce (new member; with Joe), Henry Robertson, Miss (Nettie) Shay. Hank Duryee (Central Falls livery driver). Mr. Hiram Baker (farmer, landlord near Central Falls). Sam (red-haired barefoot boy, son of neighbor farmer); Sim Rolinson (postmaster). Captain Watson (tug *Nama*), Captain Wiltsey (tug *Bohio*), Ramo (educated Indian guide), Captain Martail (Brazilian steamer captain, relative of Alcando). General George W. Goethals (chief engineer, mentioned). Rex = the runaway horse.

**Villain:** Vigues Alcando, a Spaniard/South American (Equatorial Railroad / Brazilian railroad connection), calls himself a pupil; card name "Vigues Alcando." Had a visitor (cigar smoke) at hotel; had brass-bound ticking box ("alarm clock," actually electrical timer for dynamite). Secret balcony conference at Colon with someone ("Are you sure the machine works right?").

**Events in order:**
1. Blake and Joe return on motor cycle to Hiram Baker's farm near Central Falls; no mail from Hadley. Runaway horse (Rex) pulls carriage with Hank Duryee and Alcando toward broken bridge over ravine (100 ft deep). Boys chase on motor cycle; cycle breaks gasoline pipe in field; they arrive too late but save carriage from falling.
2. Alcando gives card; letter from Hadley (addressed to both boys) introduces him. Letter (delayed by Sam) says: Panama trip, big slide expected in Culebra Cut, Alcando to accompany.
3. Boys decide to go. At hotel Alcando hides a box; wind blows paper: "...go to Panama, get all the pictures you can, especially the big guns...."
4. New York: Piper predicts "buried alive under a Culebra slide." Hadley: Alcando investigated and cleared.
5. Steamer *Gatun* to Colon via San Juan, Porto Rico. Ticking box found in Alcando's berth. Balcony conference at Washington Hotel, Colon.
6. Tug *Nama* (Captain Watson) through Gatun locks; near-crush by lock gates after towing locomotives fail. Jungle trip (Chagres River, Ramo guide): ants, iguanas, alligator attack on Blake, Ramo shoots it.
7. Culebra Cut; Alcando mutters "dynamite here, or at the dam." Brazilian steamer (Captain Martail) collides with *Nama* at Miraflores central pier; *Nama* sinks. Boys transfer to tug *Bohio* (Captain Wiltsey).
8. Upper lock gate accidentally opened; emergency dam saves *Bohio*; boys film it.
9. Big slide in Culebra Cut; Joe buried under slide, rescued by Blake and Alcando (Alcando helped dig). Joe unhurt beyond bruises.
10. Alcando's odd absences, failing skills, a warning from Wiltsey: rumor of dynamite on Gatun Dam that night. Boys use flashlight powder and automatic camera.
11. Boys hear ticking; find box with wires; Blake cuts wires. Alcando caught by guards; confesses: railroad stockholder's plot to scare shippers from the Canal; he planned to blame moving picture boys. Alcando escapes from prison next morning.
12. Boys later take pleasure trip; next volume "The Movie Boys Under the Sea." Blake receives letter, says he'll "soon be back" to New York.

---

## BOOK 2: "The Red Derelict" by Bertram Mitford (Methuen, London, 1904; Gutenberg #36588)

**Main characters:** Wagram Gerard Wagram (hero; Squire-to-be of Hilversea Court, Bassingham area; loves the place with "intense joy of possession"; pride; wife Mrs Wagram No. 1 died of morphia). Grantley Wagram (his father, "the old Squire," ~80, retired diplomat, iron-grey moustache). Everard Wagram (half-brother, "Butcher Ned," wastrel, from different mother; left ~10+ years earlier after scandal and felony; reputedly in Australia, later South Africa/Swaziland). Gerard (Wagram's son, ~14, at Hillside school; with Reggie Haldane). Father Gayle (family chaplain, friend). Monsignor Culham (old prelate, schoolfellow of Grantley). Haldane (Jack Haldane-like, county magistrate, ex-South Africa/Kimberley, lives near Fulkston; later reveals "Develin Hunt" = Jack Faro). Yvonne Haldane ("Sunbeam," golden-haired child-woman; cat Poogie, Angora). Reggie Haldane (son). Rundle (butler). Hood (keeper), Perrin (under keeper), Thompson (groom), Bowles (butcher).

**Delia Calmour** (eldest daughter of Major Calmour, retired army veterinary surgeon, drunkard, at Siege House, Bassingham). Siblings: Clytie (typist, schemer, slangy, serene, "Damages" nickname), Bob (clerk at Pownall and Skreet solicitors, cad), a third sister abroad (married in Australia), three younger boys at school. Address: Siege House, Bassingham.

**Other:** Warren (cycle hire, Bassingham); Gee and Vincent (cycle makers); Pownall and Skreet (solicitors); Develin Hunt (alias of Jack Faro, ex-West African trader/adventurer, "Golden Crown" hotel, Bassingham); Smith (landlord of Golden Crown); Father Sonnenbloem (German priest, Bassingham mission); Simcox and Yaxley (family solicitors in London); Captain Lawes (*Baleka* master), Mrs Colville and daughter Lily; Ransome (fourth officer), Gibson (chief officer, *Runic*); McAndrew (chief engineer); Powis (chief officer of Baleka, referenced).

**Events in order:**
1. Wagram in park at Hilversea walking, rifle; rescues Delia Calmour from blue wildebeest (brindled gnu) on road; her bicycle destroyed; Delia shoots the gnu with his rifle. Wagram tears waistcoat, hoof-cut. Delia gives address. Wagram sends Warren's bike, new Gee & Vincent bicycle.
2. Father Gayle conversation; Squire on Calmours ("A Calmour at Hilversea! Pho!").
3. Delia at Siege House; Bob proposes blackmail ("damages"); Clytie: "Capture the man."
4. Delia calls at Hilversea; Clytie's ploy. Old Calmour drunk.
5. Corpus Christi procession; Delia at chapel; lunch at Haldane's; Yvonne invited.
6. Breakfast talk of *Rhodesian* derelict report (Red Derelict, lat 10°5'N, long 16°36'W).
7. Wagram thrashes Bob (Robert Calmour) with ground-ash at gate on Swanton road for insulting Yvonne.
8. Bob's claim (£1000) on Wagram; claim on Wagram's behalf; Wagram sends cheque for £1000 to Delia (via Pownall and Skreet tried).
9. Delia returns cheque (torn), goes to Hilversea to say she had no part.
10. Newspaper: *Carboceer* sinks; survivor "Develin Hunt" (Squire realises: first wife's former husband).
11. Develin Hunt visits Squire; blackmail demand.
12. Monsignor Culham counsels (don't pay; trace past).
13. Delia returns; Clytie's typing work via Wagram; Delia's illustrated article for *The Old Country Side*.
14. Priest's hiding-place; Wagram's secret chamber shown to Delia. Ave Maria sung at chapel.
15. Develin Hunt's second visit; Squire; then Haldane kills? (no) — Develin Hunt meets Haldane at Golden Crown, Bob thrown out.
16. Develin Hunt's final demand: £25,000 cheque for undertaking. Reveals to Wagram that Wagram is not legitimate; mother had married Hunt earlier.
17. Wagram learns he is "Nobody of Nowhere"; seeks Everard; Hunt directs him to Lourenço Marques / Swaziland.
18. Delia's "fortune" by gipsy; Wagram sorts.
19. Old Squire dies (requiem). Wagram departs on quest; sails on *Baleka*, which sinks (propeller shaft snapped). Wagram alone on lifeboat chair; reaches Red Derelict; shark; finds pistol with nameplate "E.W." (Everard's). Eventually left on Red Derelict.
20. *Runic* collides with derelict; Delia (aboard, traveling home from Australia) saw Wagram; rescued. Romance; Delia loves Wagram.
21. Wagram captured by cannibal tribe ("Everard"/Butcher Ned, white renegade with scar near right eye); released; fights; flees; alone; Hunt Jack Faro (Develin Hunt) dies after revealing Everard is Butcher Ned, killed by pistol shot.
22. Wagram reads tin-case papers: marriage certificate of Develin Hunt's earlier marriage in South Africa, showing Hunt's wife was alive when Grantley's marriage happened... Hunt dies that night. Haldane witnesses.
23. Conclusion: Wagram proposes to Delia; she accepts. Red Derelict never sighted again.

**Notes on quoted lines:** "Mine!" (opening); "A Calmour at Hilversea! Pho!"; "There can't be two Develin Hunts"; "Capture the man"; "Nobody of Nowhere."
